Arithmetic-Input.description:
Two numbers combined: `{"type": "arithmetic", "operator": "multiply", "left": <25-day average volume>,
"right": 1.8}` is 1.8 times that average. Either side may be another arithmetic part.
Arithmetic-Input.title: Arithmetic

Arithmetic-Output.description:
Two numbers combined: `{"type": "arithmetic", "operator": "multiply", "left": <25-day average volume>,
"right": 1.8}` is 1.8 times that average. Either side may be another arithmetic part.
Arithmetic-Output.title: Arithmetic

Breadth.description:
How many stocks rose, fell and closed unchanged in one session, and their average change in percent, each stock
weighing the same.
Breadth.title: Breadth

Comparison-Input.description:
Two numbers compared. `crosses_above` and `crosses_below` read both sides at the latest daily bar and at the bar
before it, so `left` crossing above `right` holds only on the bar where it happened.
Comparison-Input.title: Comparison

Comparison-Output.description:
Two numbers compared. `crosses_above` and `crosses_below` read both sides at the latest daily bar and at the bar
before it, so `left` crossing above `right` holds only on the bar where it happened.
Comparison-Output.title: Comparison

ConditionGroup-Input.description: `all` holds when every condition holds, `any` when at least one does. A group may hold other groups.
ConditionGroup-Input.title: ConditionGroup

ConditionGroup-Output.description: `all` holds when every condition holds, `any` when at least one does. A group may hold other groups.
ConditionGroup-Output.title: ConditionGroup

Confirmed.description: Every write repeats the caller's confirmation in its body, so a stray or replayed request without it changes nothing.
Confirmed.title: Confirmed

DailyBarResponse.description: One completed daily bar (Ohlcv): `ts` is its session's 13:30 close in Asia/Taipei, volume is in shares.
DailyBarResponse.title: DailyBarResponse

EditableSetting.description:
A setting the administrator may change from the Web, named by its dotted path in its file. Anything not listed
stays read-only there: the environment, the broker and order mode, the score weights and thresholds, sizing and
stop-loss, the history and quote freshness, database, folders, credentials and every source URL.
EditableSetting.title: EditableSetting

EpsResponse.description: An EPS figure (Eps): it never comes without its period, kind, basis, source and fetch time.
EpsResponse.title: EpsResponse

EpsUnavailable.description: Missing EPS. It is never 0, and the report shows "Insufficient data" with the reason.
EpsUnavailable.title: EpsUnavailable

ExplanationRequest.description: One AI call explains one stock's valuation; the numbers are the domain's, the AI writes only text.
ExplanationRequest.title: ExplanationRequest

FiscalQuarter.description: A calendar-year fiscal quarter in Gregorian years. The MOPS adapter converts ROC years.
FiscalQuarter.title: FiscalQuarter

IndicatorOutput.description: One number an indicator gives. Which outputs an indicator has is IndicatorKind.outputs.
IndicatorOutput.title: IndicatorOutput

IndicatorValue.description:
One output of one of the strategy's indicators, `bars_ago` trading days before the latest daily bar.
`{"type": "indicator", "indicator_id": "ind_b", "output": "signal"}` is the MACD signal line of indicator ind_b.
IndicatorValue.title: IndicatorValue

LatestPrice.description:
The latest price: the run's realtime quote when it has one, else the latest daily close. It has no earlier
sample, so a crossing cannot read it; a crossing of daily closes reads `{"type": "market", "field": "close"}`.
LatestPrice.title: LatestPrice

ListedStockResponse.description: A listed stock (Stock). `today` is its official bar of the listing's latest session; None when it did not trade.
ListedStockResponse.title: ListedStockResponse

LockedSetting.description:
Settings the Web shows but never changes: they choose the broker, real orders, sizing and the order gates. The
score weights choose automatic orders as surely as the thresholds they are compared with, and the daily history's
freshness decides which stocks a run analyses at all.
LockedSetting.title: LockedSetting

MarketField.description: A field of one completed daily bar. Volume is in shares.
MarketField.title: MarketField

MarketIndex.description: A market index with a daily history. Yahoo Finance serves it under the symbol `sources.yahoo.index_symbols` names.
MarketIndex.title: MarketIndex

MarketValue.description:
A field of one completed daily bar, `bars_ago` trading days before the latest one.
`{"type": "market", "field": "volume", "bars_ago": 1}` is yesterday's volume in shares.
MarketValue.title: MarketValue

MovingAverageIndicator.description: `sma` averages the daily closes, `volume_sma` the daily volumes. Both include the bar they are read at.
MovingAverageIndicator.title: MovingAverageIndicator

Order.description:
The app's record of one order: the decision it executes, what went to (or was refused before)
the broker, and how it ended. OrderPreparation saves it in the `orders` table before it is sent, and OrderExecution
saves the broker's answer, whichever provider ran it.
Order.title: Order

OrderStatus.description: Order lifecycle. Each status lists the statuses that may follow it in next_statuses.
OrderStatus.title: OrderStatus

RunSummary.description: The run record (SystemStats) the trading journal saved.
RunSummary.title: RunSummary

SettingsAuditEntry.description: One save or restore: when, by which scope, from which revision to which, and the setting paths it changed. No value.
SettingsAuditEntry.title: SettingsAuditEntry

SettingsFile.description: A settings file in config/ the administrator may edit from the Web. Nothing else on disk can be named.
SettingsFile.title: SettingsFile

SignalResponse.description: A trading decision (TradeSignal) and its evidence; the AI report leaves out the model's raw answer.
SignalResponse.title: SignalResponse

SignalSource.description: Which decision path produced a signal.
SignalSource.title: SignalSource

StockReportResponse.description: One requested stock after a specific-stock analysis (StockReport), as the CLI's Stock Reports table shows it.
StockReportResponse.title: StockReportResponse

StockValuationResponse.description: One stock's valuation before any user assumption (StockValuation).
StockValuationResponse.title: StockValuationResponse

TechnicalReport.description:
Result produced by a TechnicalStrategy.

Hard failures reject the stock.
Soft failures reduce technical quality without rejecting the stock.
Observations describe optional technical signals.
TechnicalReport.title: TechnicalReport

TechnicalRule-Input.description: A condition and what passing or failing it does to the score. The name is a label: the condition alone decides.
TechnicalRule-Input.title: TechnicalRule

TechnicalRule-Output.description: A condition and what passing or failing it does to the score. The name is a label: the condition alone decides.
TechnicalRule-Output.title: TechnicalRule

TechnicalScoring.description:
Each rule's effect applies once, however many conditions it holds: a failed block_on_fail rule rejects the stock
and costs block_failure_penalty, a failed reduce_score_on_fail rule costs failure_score_reduction, and a passed
increase_score_on_pass rule adds pass_score_increase. Passing a block_on_fail rule adds nothing.
TechnicalScoring.title: TechnicalScoring

TechnicalSettings-Input.description:
One owner's strategies and which one each workflow uses: the Buzz strategy for Buzz, the active one for every
other workflow. revision counts the owner's saves, so a save from an older read is refused instead of overwriting.
TechnicalSettings-Input.title: TechnicalSettings

TechnicalSettings-Output.description:
One owner's strategies and which one each workflow uses: the Buzz strategy for Buzz, the active one for every
other workflow. revision counts the owner's saves, so a save from an older read is refused instead of overwriting.
TechnicalSettings-Output.title: TechnicalSettings

TechnicalStrategy-Input.description:
The user's formulas over named indicators, scored together. strategy_id is a stable key and name a label. An
indicator id such as ind_a never holds a parameter: changing ind_a's period changes every rule that reads ind_a,
and a rule that needs a different period reads another indicator.
TechnicalStrategy-Input.title: TechnicalStrategy

TechnicalStrategy-Output.description:
The user's formulas over named indicators, scored together. strategy_id is a stable key and name a label. An
indicator id such as ind_a never holds a parameter: changing ind_a's period changes every rule that reads ind_a,
and a rule that needs a different period reads another indicator.
TechnicalStrategy-Output.title: TechnicalStrategy

TimeInForce.description: How long an accepted order keeps working (Taiwan exchange terms).
TimeInForce.title: TimeInForce

ValuationReportResponse.description: A stock valued at the user's target P/E (ValuationReport). Scenarios exist exactly when its P/E is computable.
ValuationReportResponse.title: ValuationReportResponse

Workflow.description: The user-facing operation a run belongs to. Each run has one run id.
Workflow.title: Workflow

HTTPBearer.description: API_TOKEN for the owner's endpoints, ADMIN_API_TOKEN for /v1/admin.

info.description:
Runs the stock-agent workflows and reads what they recorded, on the same runtime as the CLI.

Scopes. Public: the built-in strategies and market data (`/v1/market`). Owner,
`Authorization: Bearer <API_TOKEN>`: every write and every read of private data (runs, decisions, orders,
watchlist, account, saved technical settings). Administrator, `Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_API_TOKEN>`: only the
settings files under `/v1/admin`. A scope whose token is unset answers 403; the administrator scope also when
ADMIN_API_TOKEN equals API_TOKEN. Every write repeats `"confirm": true` in its body.

Orders. Full Cycle, specific-stock analysis, valuation and market data never order. Buzz and Intraday send orders
through the same gates and trading journal as the CLI, and the API starts them only while the execution provider is
the mock broker (403 otherwise). No endpoint places, cancels or modifies an order by itself, and the API offers no
manual BUY.

Workflows run in the background, one at a time per server: a start answers 202 with the run id, and
GET /v1/runs/{run_id} reports the run's state and its record. Run the server with one worker process.
info.title: TW-Stock-Alpha-Agent

The owner's strategies and which one each workflow uses, with the revision a save must carry. The first read

Replaces the owner's settings as a whole, for the next workflow. Invalid settings save nothing and answer 422 with
one error per field under body.settings. Settings read before another save answer 409 and save nothing: read
them again, reapply the change, and save with the new revision.

fair price. With `technical`, the survivors then go through the owner's active strategy, which loads their daily
history. No AI call.

post.description:
Adds listed stocks to the MANUAL watchlist, as menu 4 does after an analysis. An unlisted ID adds nothing at all and
answers 422; an unavailable listing answers 503.
Takes stocks off the MANUAL watchlist only. A TECHNICAL or BUZZ entry of the same stock stays until it expires.
Answers each text message in a LINE webhook call. A call without LINE's signature over its body is refused.
